external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The source does not place colleagues in a single trust zone.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store who uses their own identity provider for sign-in.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which franchise colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies group membership changes and leaver information to the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for their sign-in.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, accepts franchise identity-provider sign-in, supplies public signing material, and writes sign-ins to the audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: Tokens are valid for twelve hours. There is no way to revoke a token before it expires. Nothing calls back to the broker to ask whether a colleague is still allowed in. The source does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application running on the corporate network that allows holders of a token containing the store-manager group to change prices and void transactions across every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications. It also runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker to sign tokens.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and the groups they are in.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Group membership comes from the HR system overnight. The source does not state whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. The source does not state whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: vouch for sign-in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague uses their own identity provider for sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.notes: The source does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a colleague after sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in. Tokens are good for twelve hours and cannot be pulled back before they expire.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: provide token
data_flows.description: The identity broker provides a token that the store admin console uses to decide what the holder may do.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.notes: The console uses the store-manager group to permit price changes and transaction voids. Nothing calls back to the broker to check whether the colleague is still allowed in.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the signing key from the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of token signing key

data_flows.name: keep signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps the token signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: provide membership changes
data_flows.description: The HR system provides overnight group-membership and leaver changes to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The source says the broker pulls the changes once a night, so the broker initiates this interaction.

data_flows.name: maintain directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains colleague and group records in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise-store environment associated with franchise colleagues and their own identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

trust_boundaries.name: home devices
trust_boundaries.description: The home-device environment from which colleagues may sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home
trust_boundaries.notes: The source mentions home devices as a sign-in location but does not name a specific device or component placed there.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it contains colleague records, staff-related identity information, and group membership.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory keeps colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log contains personal information because it records sign-ins associated with colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds the token signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker keeps a signing key in the key store.
